newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says EMU criteria not negotiable.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says EMU criteria not negotiable.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, in the text of speech to be delivered on Friday, said the fiscal criteria for Europe's planned single currency were not negotiable and that the timetable must be maintained.

According to a summary of the speech distributed by the federal press office, Kohl said that any discussion on which European Union members would qualify for monetary union or whether Germany would qualify was superfluous.

Kohl said European economic and monetary union (EMU) would create a currency bloc that would improve the ability of European companies to compete against firms whose business was conducted in dollars or yen.
"It is agreed that the stability criteria in the Maastricht treaty are not up for negotiation. Likewise the timetable for the common European currency must be observed," Kohl said.
"Current speculation over who will qualify for monetary union and whether Germany will meet the stability criteria is superfluous," he added.
The Maastricht treaty states that EMU participants must meet a range of fiscal criteria, including limits on budget deficits and public debt.
Few EU member states meet the criteria now. Germany failed to meet all of them last year and runs the risk of missing the key deficit criterion this year.
The participants in the first round of EMU in 1999 will be chosen early next year based on fiscal performance data from 1997.
Kohl was speaking at the 25th anniversary of the founding of SAP AG, the German software group that has become a world leader in business software and Europe's largest software maker.
